title: Coordinate Geometry of Straight Lines
seo_title: Coordinate Geometry – SSS 3 Mathematics Worksheets with Answers (NERDC)
standard_text: Find the distance between two points, the midpoint and the gradient of a line; find the equation of a straight line; use parallel and perpendicular lines. (summary of the NERDC SSS 3 Mathematics curriculum)
meta_desc: Free SSS 3 maths worksheets on coordinate geometry: distance, midpoint, gradient, equation of a line, parallel and perpendicular lines. 100 questions with answers.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • Distance = √((x₂ − x₁)² + (y₂ − y₁)²). Midpoint = ((x₁ + x₂)/2, (y₁ + y₂)/2).
  • The equation of a line is y = mx + c, or y − y₁ = m(x − x₁) through (x₁, y₁).
  • Parallel lines have equal gradients; perpendicular gradients multiply to −1.

Examples

Example

A(1, 2), B(7, 10)

Gradient 8/6

Distance √(36 + 64)

Answer: m = 4/3, AB = 10

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Subtracting in a different order on top and bottomKeep the same order.
Forgetting the negative reciprocalPerpendicular to 2 is −1/2.
Adding in the distance formulaSubtract the coordinates.

items.q: P(1, 2), A(2, 3) and B(0, 3) are the vertices of a triangle. Which statement is true?
c: PA² + PB² = AB², so angle APB = 90°
PA = PB = AB, so the triangle is equilateral
AB² + PA² = PB², so angle PAB = 90°
items.e: PA² = 2, PB² = 2 and AB² = 4. 2 + 2 = 4, so by the converse of Pythagoras' theorem angle APB = 90°.

items.q: Find the area of the triangle with vertices (−2, −4), (−1, −4) and (1, 2).
items.e: The base is on the line y = −4 with length −1 − (−2) = 1. The height is 6. Area = ½ × 1 × 6 = 3 square units.
